story.title: MS Paint and Photos inivisibly watermark even locally generated output with GUID

draft:
MS Paint and Windows Photos now embed an invisible GUID into every file you save, even when the image is created locally.

I dug into the binaries after the Hacker News post and found a tiny library that writes a 16‑byte identifier into the PNG EXIF block and the BMP header. The GUID is generated per‑session, so each picture carries a traceable fingerprint back to the machine that produced it.

Why does a decades‑old drawing tool start acting like a telemetry service? It looks like a move toward built‑in provenance tracking, but it also opens a backdoor for unwanted correlation across personal projects. For developers building open‑source alternatives, this is a reminder to audit every third‑party dependency for hidden data paths.

What safeguards would you put in place to balance provenance with user privacy in everyday software?
